title: Make D2 renders reproducible and keep verification builds off the dev server
description:
Two build-tooling defects found while re-rendering the diagrams for the
newsprint palette.

## D2 renders were not reproducible, so the CI drift check could not pass

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` installs the pinned d2 v0.7.1, runs
`make diagrams`, then `git diff --exit-code` against the committed SVGs.
That check can never have passed: d2 picks a **random CSS scope id** per
run (`.d2-4009697037` -> `.d2-1836642998`) and embeds it in every rule, so
two renders of unchanged sources differed by roughly 900 lines.

Fix: pass `--salt "${name}"` in `scripts/render-diagrams.sh`. That pins the
id, and salting per diagram also keeps ids distinct when several diagrams
are embedded in one page — which is the case on the architecture page.
Verified by rendering twice and diffing: byte-identical.

On the version pin itself — it is load-bearing, not paranoia. The pin in
the script mirrors the one in CI, and that is what makes the drift check
meaningful. Homebrew only ships 0.9.0, which would produce SVGs that fail
CI. To move versions, bump `D2_VERSION` and the `ci.yml` install together
and re-render in the same commit.

## A verification build silently breaks a running dev server

`next build` and `next dev` share `.next`, so a build run against a live
dev server replaces the dev manifests and leaves it serving Next's
fallback shell — every route answering 200 with none of the site's content
in it, which looks like a broken page rather than a stopped server. I did
this to my own dev server twice during this work.

Partial mitigation: `distDir: process.env.NEXT_DIST_DIR || '.next'` in
`site/next.config.js` allows building aside.

**Caveat, and the reason this card exists:** the build that broke the
server the second time was itself run with `NEXT_DIST_DIR` set, so that
guard demonstrably does not fully protect `.next`. I did not chase the
cause, since confirming it means deliberately breaking a dev server the
user is working in. Until someone does, treat the operational rule as the
real protection: **do not run `next build` in a worktree while its dev
server is up.** Stop it, build, restart.

## Files

- `scripts/render-diagrams.sh` — `--salt`
- `site/next.config.js` — `distDir`

Branch `feat/newsprint-brand-lockup`, not yet merged.
